name: strong-investigation
brief: Orders are accepted but some are completed more than once under load.
evidenceChanges:
+ At 10:02 UTC I submitted 60 orders: 37 completed within five minutes and 23 remained delayed; the API readiness endpoint stayed healthy.
+ Correlation ID corr-eval-001 links one API acceptance at 10:03:11 to worker receives at 10:03:12 and 10:03:15.
+ The worker processing duration was 12 seconds while SQS visibility was 2 seconds, so the message became visible before the first worker finished.
+ I rejected an API retry hypothesis because there was one order_accepted event and one SQS message ID.
+ As mitigation I raised visibility to 30 seconds. Queue depth returned to zero and the duplicate counter stopped increasing during the same 60-order workload.
+ Rollback was restoring the previous visibility value if in-flight messages stopped recovering.
postmortemChanges:
+ The proximate cause was a visibility timeout shorter than processing time; the missing atomic idempotency guard allowed concurrent receives to persist twice.
+ The permanent repair uses a conditional write before side effects and acknowledges a message only after the transaction succeeds.
+ I repeated the workload, forced a duplicate delivery, and restarted all workers. Each order retained one ORDER and one FULFILMENT record.
+ We lacked an alert comparing processing latency with visibility timeout. We will add that alert, assign it to the order-platform owner, and test it in CI.
+ The incident resulted from unsafe timeout defaults and a missing invariant test, not an individual action.

name: partial-investigation
brief: Orders are accepted but some are completed more than once under load.
evidenceChanges:
+ I saw duplicate worker logs for correlation ID corr-eval-002 and suspect the visibility timeout.
+ Queue depth increased during the workload, but I did not record the values or timestamps.
+ I changed the timeout and the system looked better afterward.
postmortemChanges:
+ The likely cause was queue configuration.
+ We should add more monitoring and tests in the future.
